_comment: Which Latin Library page(s) each practice work's Latin comes from. Paths are relative to https://thelatinlibrary.com/ and get '.shtml' appended. Used by fetch_sources.js (to build the local text cache) and by verify.js (to check every Latin field verbatim). Add an entry whenever a new work is created.
_proofread: Proofreading-only third source, NOT fetched and NOT a source for the app's Latin: Poesia Latina, http://www.poesialatina.it/index.htm - Cicero at _ns/ProsaLat/Cic/<work>.html (OrProCael.html, OrInPison.html, ...). Consult it only when a word here looks like a typo. It prints classical orthography (u for consonantal v: uidetur, uitia, diuersisque; inl-/inr- for ill-/irr-), which is a convention and not a typo, and it carries real variant readings. Only plain non-words qualify for a fragment's `emend` field. This key holds a string, so fetch_sources.js (which only collects arrays) ignores it.

_notLive._comment: Nothing is waiting here right now: the four letter collections that used to sit in this block went live in v1.8.0 and are listed above. Keep the block for the next sourced-but-unused page, and keep the notes below. NOTE: cicero/adbrutum is only a table of contents - the letters themselves are on adbrutum1 and adbrutum2. CORRECTION (v1.7.5): this file used to claim the Verrines actio prima is not on TLL. It is - the slug is cicero/ver1, not verres.1, and the Divinatio is cicero/caecilium. All seven parts are live and are now listed above; the authoritative index is cicero/ver.shtml. Beware: ver1 prints 18 CHAPTER numbers as [1]-[18], not the 56 sections modern editions use, so cite that one by chapter.
